text:
- [LLOG.11.9] **A `logical` emit whose activation ends inside its own
  firing is a compile error** (`DS_VALIDATE_LOGICAL_EMIT_SELF_ENDING`).
  The body of an `after` clause is such a place, and the compiler must
  refuse a `logical` emit there: the body runs in the follow-up rule, which
  matches the timer fact and retracts it ([LTAC.3.4]). The timer is that
  rule's only pattern, so the match is gone before the firing ends.

  **So is a rule's RHS after a `withdraw` of one of its bindings.** `withdraw b` removes a fact the activation matched
  ([LSCO.4.5.9]), so the match is gone from that action on. The compiler must
  refuse a `logical` emit that follows a `withdraw` in the same RHS, at the
  emit, naming the `withdraw`. An emit before the `withdraw` is not refused:
  its fact is justified while the match holds, and the `withdraw` ends that
  justification ([LLOG.15.1]). A body nested in a later action is not this
  RHS. It runs in a rule of its own, a continuation rule ([LCCO.5.2]) or an
  `after` follow-up, and the `withdraw` does not end that rule's match;
  [LGRA.10.1.3] says what such a body may read.

  **So is a rule's RHS from an emit that replaces a fact the activation
  matched.** Take an emit of schema `X` where the
  rule binds `b` to a positive `X` pattern, every identity-key slot of the emit
  ([LFAC.1.7]) is the same slot of `b` (`id: b.id`), and some other slot of the
  emit is a literal that differs from the literal the pattern requires of that
  slot, as [LCYC.6.1.2] compares them. That emit is a meaningful change to
  `b`'s fact and replaces it ([LFAC.2.5.3]), so the match is gone from that
  action on, as after `withdraw b`. The compiler must refuse such an emit when
  it is `logical`, and a `logical` emit that follows such an emit in the same
  RHS, at the emit, naming the one that replaced the fact. A replacement that
  only run-time values decide is not refused here; [LLOG.15.1] governs it.

  A fact emitted in any of these places is withdrawn as it is made: the activation that
  justified it has ended, so justification withdrawal retracts it in the
  same firing ([LLOG.15.1]). Accepting the program would give an author a
  fact that never exists, or — on a runtime that skipped the withdrawal —
  one that no live activation supports and nothing ever retracts.

  **What the author writes instead.** A plain `emit` is not the answer: a
  plain emit requires a `ttl` schema ([LFAC.1.3.1]), and `emit X logical`
  requires `X` to be declared `logical` ([LLOG.11.1]), so the choice is
  between the two lifetimes rather than between two spellings of one. The
  derived fact is expressed by emitting a `ttl` fact from the deferred body
  and joining it to the condition that should keep the logical fact alive:
  a second rule matching both emits the `logical` fact, and its justifying
  activation is that rule's, which lives exactly as long as the join holds.
  After a `withdraw`, the fact the author wants is likewise a `ttl` or
  `explicit` fact, or a `logical` fact that another rule's join justifies.
